correctness.rationale: Assume rho,delta,phi,k>0 and B=(a+k/rho)/delta>0, compact invariant mu. Stationarity of x^2/2 gives E[xy]=E[x^2]=q, and z gives zbar=phi*q. From w^2/2 and x*w obtain E[xw]=0, E[yw]=(k/rho)q. From y^2/2, E[xyz]=((a+k/rho)/delta)q=B*q. From z^2/2, E[z^2]=phi*B*q=B*zbar; hence Var(z)=zbar(B-zbar) and 0<=zbar<=B. If zbar=0 then x=0 support, invariance forces y=w=0, and only compact complete orbit of z prime=-z is z=0: origin Dirac. If zbar=B, variance zero forces z=B and xy=B/phi>0 on support. Compactness and continuity give x sign constant and |x| bounded below, forcing w prime=-k*x to be unbounded, contradiction. At source parameters rho=10,a=296.5,delta=40,phi=10,k=8, B=2973/400 and q<2973/4000. This is an exact necessary stationary law and does not claim a nontrivial stationary measure exists.
residual_risks: The parabola is a necessary relation only; nontrivial invariant-measure existence and sharp attainment are not demonstrated.
